newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-CARDS HOPE TO HAVE FULL DECK AGAINST BRAVES' DEALERS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-CARDS HOPE TO HAVE FULL DECK AGAINST BRAVES' DEALERS.

text.p: The Cards will be playing with a full deck against the daunting dealers of the Braves pitching staff with the news that Ray Lankford will be in the lineup for Wednesday's opener of their league championship series.

Lankford, who two weeks ago tore the rotator cuff in his throwing shoulder, will start in centre field for the St Louis Cardinals who take on the World Series champion Atlanta Braves in a best-of-seven series for the National League title.
"I'm not going to be 100 percent," he said after working out indoors at Atlanta-Fulton County Stadium Monday. "I can't throw the ball the way I'd like to to, but I can throw it."
Lankford batted .275 with 21 homers and 86 runs batted in this season.

The Cards, who swept San Diego in their divisional series, have other walking wounded in the lineup as they prepare for the Braves, who have ridden their awesome starting pitching to a record-tying fifth straight league championship appearance.
The rotation of John Smoltz, Greg Maddux and Tom Glavine has led the Braves to a league championship series run matched only by the Oakland Athletics from 1971 to 1975.
St Louis manager Tony La Russa, who managed the last World Series team from Oakland in 1990, hopes he does not have to shuffle the Cards' lineup with any more injury setbacks.

Slugging left fielder Ron Gant also (30 homers, 82 RBI) tore his rotator cuff in August, but not to his throwing shoulder. Power-hitting third baseman Gary Gaetti (23 homers, 80 RBI) bruised his right heel and sprained the ankle in the Padres series but is determined to play.
The Cardinals, who will start Andy Benes (18-10, 3.83 ERA) in the opener, will need all their offensive weapons against Atlanta and their all-time great staff.

Atlanta will open with Smoltz, who was 24-8 with a 2.95 ERA during the regular season and is an odds-on favourite to register an extraordinary sixth successive Cy Young Award for members of the Braves staff.
Smoltz will be followed by Maddux (15-11, 2.72), the Cy Young winner the last three seasons with the Braves and the season before that with the Chicago Cubs, and 1991 recipient Glavine (15-10, 2.98).

The terrific trio throttled the Dodgers in their three-game divisional series sweep, limiting them to two earned runs in 22 2/3 innings (0.79 ERA) and 12 hits. Los Angeles batted a paltry .149 against them.
The Braves needed all that good pitching as they batted only .180 in the division series themselves.
They hope to get their three big run producers -- Chipper Jones (30 homers, 110 RBI), Fred McGriff (28 homers, 107 RBI) and Ryan Klesko (34 homers, 93 RBI) -- untracked.
